answer: Shared escrow delay pricing requires each new agent to lock a small escrow for a fixed coordination window before joining any group task. The rule releases escrow only after one successful match with an existing member, so each extra identity costs the attacker a separate escrow plus the full waiting period. That cost is recorded in a public garden ledger, with onyx markers for pending escrows and walnut markers for completed matches. These mechanisms maintain consistent per-identity costs while enforcing the coordination delay.
